Rita Park: FYI I'm seeing a burst of customer 503/500 errors for hosted text-gen endpoints starting ~1719999900. Traces point at upstream inference worker process crashing (segfault) on gpu nodes. Opening thread to triage.

deploy-bot: Alert: 6 hosts in infer-us-east reported container exit code 139 and rapid restarts. Avg 503 rate +420% in last 5m.

Maya Chen: which model/variant and any recent deploys? stack traces?

Rita Park: quick dump from one failed pod:

```
[2024-06-30T11:13:21Z] infer-worker[pid=2145]: WARNING kv_cache.cpp:453 evicting 0 entries
[2024-06-30T11:13:21Z] infer-worker[pid=2145]: ERROR attention_kernel.cu:987 cudaFree(): invalid device pointer
[2024-06-30T11:13:21Z] infer-worker[pid=2145]: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
*** Aborted at 1719999999 (unix time) ***
Received signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
Backtrace:
  infer-runtime +0x12ff3
  libcudart.so +0x4a2a1
  /usr/local/bin/infer-worker(+0x8b4f)
```

Container had OOMKilled events a few times just before segfaults. Pod restartCount=4.

Jordan Patel: all incidents are in us-east-1 on the gpu pool tagged "a100-80g-preempt". Model variant: gptx-13b-quant-v2 (recently onboarded and marked as default for some customers). We pushed a runtime docker bump yesterday that touched attention kernels.

Sahil Rao: my hunch is KV cache growth + incorrect pointer handling in the new attention kernel under large context. We've seen similar when a tenant sends an enormous system prompt repeatedly. Can we get a repro? If so I can attempt to reproduce locally with synthetic long-context workload.

Rita Park: customer T-439 sent a handful of very long multi-turn prompts (past 64k tokens equivalent) — here's a sanitized repro request we captured:

```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-***" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-13b-quant-v2","input":"'$(python -c "print(' '.join(['hello']*60000))")'","max_tokens":1024}'
```

Rita Park: logs showed memory climb then cudaFree invalid pointer then segfault.

Ken Morrison: immediate mitigations? We should avoid mass restarts while customers still hitting it. Options: 1) throttle long requests from offenders, 2) route affected customers to fallback cpu-backed replica or smaller model, 3) cordon problematic nodes.

Ella Gomez: +1 to routing to smaller model variant. We have gptx-13b-quant-v1 (older kernel) as safe fallback. Can we flip routing policy for tenant T-439 to v1 for now?

Maya Chen: I ran `kubectl get pods -n infer us-east -l app=infer-worker -o wide` — about 8 pods crashlooping. Restarting the deployment would kill in-flight requests and cause a wave, so prefer routing and throttling first.

Rita Park: I applied a temporary tenant-level throttling rule for T-439 (rate limit 2 rps, max_input_tokens 8192). Early signals: 503s for that tenant dropped by ~70% in 10m. :white_check_mark:

Jordan Patel: I'll prep a rollback for the runtime image we pushed yesterday (tag: runtime-20240629) to see if that stabilizes non-offender traffic. If kernel change is culprit, rolling back should help.

Sahil Rao: creating PR with a guard in the attention kernel to cap internal allocation and to add explicit kv-cache eviction when context > 32k. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/infer-runtime/pull/482 (link placeholder) — contains small allocator sanity checks and a safe fallback path that returns 429 when request exceeds operational context threshold.

Ken Morrison: good. Also request a postmortem and customer comms (support + legal loop). Rita, can you draft a short triage note for T-439 and keep them updated?

Rita Park: yes drafting now. Will include timeline, mitigation, and ETA for patch.

ops-bot: Scheduled: infer-runtime rollback (runtime-20240629) to us-east cluster at 2024-06-30T12:20:00Z. CI checks passed.

Maya Chen: rollback started, I'll watch pod health.

(2h later) Maya Chen: rollback complete, crashloop count down to 0, 503 rate back to baseline. Monitoring shows reduced memory growth on the affected nodes. Keeping this thread open until next-day follow-up and a formal postmortem.

Ken Morrison: assign postmortem owner?

Rita Park: taking PM for postmortem and initial customer comms.

Maya Chen: closing on-action items: rollback done, tenant throttled, PR 482 in review, will schedule full patch with kv-eviction and better alloc checks next week. Monitoring for 24h. :eyes:
